hints: Look closely at the left-hand end of molecule X. How many of the three glycerol carbons are still carrying free OH groups, and how many are joined to a long fatty acid tail?
Find the link between glycerol and the fatty acid tail (C-O-C=O). What type of bond is this, and check the fatty acid chain for any C=C double bonds to decide if it is saturated.
walkthrough:
**Spot the glycerol backbone in molecule X**

Look at the left side. You can see three carbons in a row, which is glycerol. Two of them still have free OH groups, and only one is joined to the long chain on the right. That tells you only one fatty acid has been attached.

**Identify the bond and the type of fatty acid**

The join is -O-C=O, which is an ester bond formed by condensation. So molecule X has one ester bond. Now check the long tail. Every carbon has maximum hydrogens and only single C-C bonds, so it is a saturated fatty acid, not unsaturated.

**Recall a triglyceride for comparison**

A triglyceride is glycerol with all three OH groups esterified. So it always contains three fatty acids and three ester bonds. That matches one fatty acid in X and three fatty acids in a triglyceride.

options.A: Molecule X has a saturated fatty acid (no C=C), and a triglyceride can contain saturated or unsaturated fatty acids, not only saturated.
options.B: Molecule X does have one ester bond where the fatty acid joins glycerol, so it is not correct to say no ester bonds.
options.C: Molecule X is a monoglyceride with one fatty acid joined to glycerol, while a triglyceride has three fatty acids joined to glycerol.
options.D: Molecule X has only one fatty acid tail, not two, so counting two fatty acids is incorrect.
